note_sections.t: Re-evaluation for prostate cancer treatment decision following stable Gleason 3+4 diagnosis and rising PSA trend.

Long-standing referral for prostate cancer management. Patient is a 65-year-old graphic designer, married, and resides in a multi-generational household with his adult child. He reports mild lower urinary tract symptoms with an IPSS score of 2. He cycles twice weekly for approximately 20 km and consumes 10 units of alcohol per week. He is a current smoker with a 24 pack-year history and takes paracetamol as needed for osteoarthritis. No recent other appointments. PSA has risen from 2.6 ng/mL in May 2023 to 12.4 ng/mL in February 2025.

On DRE, the prostate is non-palpable with no nodules or asymmetry, consistent with clinical stage cT1c. General examination reveals a well-nourished man with stable vital signs, BP 149/75 mmHg, HR 61 bpm. No lymphadenopathy or abdominal masses detected.
